# Remove-ZbxCepRule

## SYNOPSIS

Removes event processing rules.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxCepRule [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixCepRule>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An event processing rule matches incoming events against a filter within a time window and applies its operations to them, in sort order (Zabbix 8.0 and later). The Remove-ZbxCepRule cmdlet deletes the event processing rules given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with ceprule.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete an event processing rule

```powershell
Remove-ZbxCepRule -InputObject 'Tag web alerts' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the event processing rule Tag web alerts. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the event processing rules a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxCepRule -Name 'Tag*' | Remove-ZbxCepRule -WhatIf
```

Lists the event processing rules whose names start with Tag that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
